headline: Frontend engineer focused on UI and UX. I ship end-to-end features when needed, and own the build and CI tooling around them.
highlightsIntro: Many of these ran in production for years, where money or decisions happen: ads, paywalls, club cards, whole portal frontends. Several started the same way: little context, important work in flight, and taking over the operation.

highlights.title: Leadership and mentoring
highlights.summary: Led and mentored the third-party frontend developers who joined the team, one of them for over a year.
bullets: Onboarded them to the team's standards and legacy codebases, with daily syncs and pull request reviews.
Taught incident handling across development, homologation and production, and handed over real ownership as they grew.
Shared a git and conflict study that improved how we worked as a pair.

highlights.title: Internal hosting platform
highlights.summary: Designed and built a self-service platform to host the company's internal apps, from the first idea to the first live apps.
bullets: One reverse proxy and one port: each app gets its own path and container, published by its own pipeline.
Routes are validated before going live and roll back automatically on failure.
Aligned management and infrastructure to make it happen; the first apps run on it, and more teams are lined up.
A clean-room public version is in progress: [drail](https://github.com/pedrovanzo/drail).

highlights.title: AI as a multiplier
highlights.summary: The point where AI became a multiplier: faster learning, faster delivery, wider reach.
bullets: Learned [Docker](https://www.docker.com) in a 13-level hands-on project, which became the base of the hosting platform.
Built an autonomous coding loop ([Ralph loop](https://ghuntley.com/ralph/)) from scratch, sandboxed in a container, and a game review app to exercise it.
Work the same way every time: brainstorm, grill, spec, then build in vertical slices with AI, reviewing every change.
tags: Claude Code workspace / dev tooling setup

highlights.title: Shared component packages and design tokens
highlights.summary: Founded and owned the architecture of the shared component packages behind [A Gazeta](https://www.agazeta.com.br), [HZ](https://www.agazeta.com.br/hz), [Correio da Bahia](https://www.correio24horas.com.br) and [Roma News](https://www.romanews.com.br).
bullets: Built the first full component set: site chrome and article building blocks.
Designed a design-token system so one package could style every portal, then planned its move to brand-neutral names with a teammate.
Introduced [Tailwind](https://tailwindcss.com) and a faster build; the packages still run Correio da Bahia and Roma News in production (as of Nov 16, 2026).

Checkable in public archives: the token classes show up in the portals' pages, e.g. [Roma News, Jul 2024](https://web.archive.org/web/20240702203345/https://romanews.com.br/) (the original brand names), [Correio da Bahia, Nov 2024](https://web.archive.org/web/20241101000917/https://correio24horas.com.br/) (after the rename) and [A Gazeta, Mar 2026](https://web.archive.org/web/20260301000239/https://agazeta.com.br/).

highlights.title: Stepping into ad-tech ownership
highlights.summary: Years of ad and Core Web Vitals work paid off when the ad-tech setup was left without an owner.
bullets: Hundreds of ad-related changes across nine repositories: one base set of CSS rules tailored to each portal, with reserved slot heights to avoid layout shift.
Fine-tuned [AMP](https://amp.dev) pages by hand until they passed Google's validation.
In 2026, became the developer support for a rebuilt ad team: GTM and GAM setups, a new interstitial format and metric-driven fixes.

highlights.title: Correio da Bahia redesign
highlights.summary: Led the redesign of [Correio da Bahia](https://www.correio24horas.com.br)'s portal as its main frontend developer, from the client's intentions to the cutover.
bullets: Turned non-technical requests from the newspaper's staff into development decisions, with the designer.
Proposed and iterated a new typography system until it was approved; it's still in production (as of Nov 16, 2026).
Delegated smaller tasks to a paired developer.

highlights.title: AI voice MVP
highlights.summary: Came up with an AI voice solution in a company innovation program and built the MVP.
bullets: Showed a cloned voice reading an article; compliance was notified first, and only consenting employees' voices were used.
Affiliate sites without enough staff to voice their articles adopted the solution.

lessons: In a product as large as a CMS there's no small scope: time spent scoping costs less than patching later.
Not all debt is technical: disorganized requirements create planning debt, and code can't pay it off.
Shared packages need shared rules: with three businesses on one package, one portal's change hits the other two.
One package manager, one lockfile: mixed setups only show their drift on a broken deploy.
